speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: When the two men enquired about adopting a child, they were advised that the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) was unlikely to recommend the adoption of children by parties who were in a same-sex relationship.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Both of them then went to the United States (US) for commercial surrogacy and paid a total of US$200,000 to a private company there.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Under the terms of the surrogacy contract, the arrangement was for the surrogate mother to carry the baby to term, deliver him and then give up her rights over him.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The child was born in 2013 and was handed over to the applicant and his partner.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The child is a US citizen and has been brought up in Singapore by the two of them in the same household.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The applicant later applied to Court to adopt the child.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In February 2017, the Family Justice Court ruled against the adoption.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The applicant then appealed to the High Court.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Following the ruling, the applicant and his partner gave media interviews, reported locally and abroad, describing the challenges that same-sex parents faced when wanting to conceive and raise their own children in Singapore, and shared about the process they went through to start a family in Singapore via overseas surrogacy.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Understandably, the High Court's decision to grant the appeal has evoked a diverse range of emotions and reactions amongst Singaporeans and raised questions about the implications of this case.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: First, around the definition of marriage, family and future conceptions of family in society, some Singaporeans are concerned whether this ruling sets a precedent to allow homosexual couples to legally adopt children in Singapore and, in so doing, mainstreams same-sex parent households here.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Others, including lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender (LGBT) activists, say that this case is a step towards the recognition and legalisation of same-sex relationships.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Second, on commercial surrogacy, some have asked whether this ruling legitimises commercial surrogacy carried out overseas, especially in light of the complex ethical questions surrounding this practice.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Members' questions today reflect this range of views and reactions.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Indeed, these emerging issues and divergent attitudes have become increasingly salient in our society.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: LGBT persons have a place here in Singapore and are entitled to their own private lives.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Just like other Singaporeans, they have access to opportunities and social support, such as education, employment and healthcare, and should, like all Singaporeans, not be subject to prejudice and discrimination.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: However, we must be mindful that a push for rights and entitlements which the broader society is not ready for, or able to accept, will provoke a pushback, and can be very socially divisive.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: A push to use legislation or the Courts to precipitate social change involving issues as deeply held and personal as this polarises society.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: While we recognise that there are increasingly diverse forms of families and households in Singapore, the prevailing social norm in our society is still that of a man and woman marrying and having and bringing up children within a stable family unit.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This is also the family structure that the Government encourages.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Most of us would agree that it is ideal for children to grow up in families anchored by strong and stable marriages.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This is reflected in the differentiation we maintain in policies and benefits to encourage and support parenthood within marriage.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: It follows from this that the Government does not encourage planned and deliberate single parenthood as a lifestyle choice.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Specifically, we do not support the use of Assisted Reproduction Technology or surrogacy by singles to conceive children, for the purpose of forming single unwed parent households.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Hence, In-Vitro Fertilisation or other Assisted Reproduction Procedures at licensed assisted reproduction institutions are available in Singapore only to married couples who experience difficulties in natural conception.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Over time, social attitudes have evolved to greater accommodation of homosexuals.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The Government's policy is not to intrude or interfere with the private lives of Singaporeans, including homosexuals and their relationships or partnerships.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In raising this objection, MSF had carefully considered the welfare of the boy.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: First, the child is not stateless but is a citizen of the US.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Second, the child remains with the father and will be cared for.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The father has full parental rights and responsibilities, even if the adoption was not granted.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In fact, the Women's Charter obliges parents to provide for their children, regardless of the children’s legitimacy status.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The High Court stated that they had reached their decision in this case "with not insignificant difficulty".

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The Court affirmed the public policy against the formation of same-sex family units and recognised that granting the adoption would violate it.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This was, however, weighed against the interest of the child's welfare.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: For instance, while the welfare of the child should always be a very important consideration in adoption proceedings, we are looking at whether the Adoption of Children Act needs to be amended so that a better balance can be struck when important public policy considerations are involved.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We are also studying the issue of surrogacy carefully.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This is a complex issue with ethical, social, health and legal implications for all parties involved.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: For commercial surrogacy in particular, concerns have been raised about the exploitation of women and commodification of children.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: These issues are not trivial and warrant careful study and discussion.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Persons who are considering surrogacy should take this into account from the outset while making their decision, as such factors could have a significant impact on the child.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Today, surrogacy cannot be carried out in Singapore at any licensed healthcare institution that provides assisted reproduction services.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Parents who have gone overseas for surrogacy and who come back to apply for adoption of their surrogate children will have their applications assessed on a case-by-case basis.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: They will also be scrutinised by the Courts during the adoption hearings.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: These children were all born to married couples applying jointly to adopt their child, and who had resorted to surrogacy because the couples were infertile.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Access to housing will continue to be determined by prevailing criteria, in line with public policy supporting parenthood within marriage.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: All Singaporean children, regardless of their legitimacy status, will receive Government benefits that support their growth and development, including healthcare and education benefits.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Commercial surrogacy, in my view, where a woman's womb is rented for money, is demeaning to the child and to the woman.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Life is formed for a commercial price, then bought and sold.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: My supplementary questions are: would the Minister agree, for these reasons, that commercial surrogacy should be prohibited?

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Further, it can be argued that a substantial amount of commercial surrogacy is undertaken by women who are poverty-stricken and it is, therefore, exploitative of them.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: So, my second question is, for those additional reasons, does the Minister agree that commercial surrogacy should be barred?

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Thirdly, to make these principles even clearer, could the Minister consider amendments to the Children and Young Persons Act, the Penal Code and the Adoption Act?

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: And I am very willing to work with MSF, as a Member of Parliament, to make the necessary amendments in the law to reflect those principles.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Surrogacy is an issue that is fraught with ethical concerns.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The Member has rightly pointed out that some have argued against the commodification of children, against the exploitation of women.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And others, on the other hand, say that this offers a way out for couples who are otherwise unable to bear their own children.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Some women, for instance, have, due to medical reasons, had their wombs removed.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And even though they get married and wish to have their own children, are unable to do so, and that could be why some of them go overseas and undergo surrogacy.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But where couples for whatever reason go overseas and come back, it is scrutinised on a case-by-case basis, ultimately with the gatekeeping by the Courts, who will look at the application.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Thus far, all surrogate adoptions have been by married couples, men and women who have had medical reasons why they cannot otherwise conceive and these are then assessed by the Courts holistically.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: As to whether we should completely prohibit surrogacy by Singaporeans within Singapore or all over the world, and whether we should amend the legislation to do so, it is something that we must consider holistically and carefully, keeping in mind the wishes, aspirations and concerns of mothers who would otherwise not be able to conceive their own flesh and blood.

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: I note that the Ministry will be reviewing the adoption framework on a more generic basis, but with specifics to the case itself, can I just find out whether the Ministry will be involved at all in monitoring or surveillance of this child during his growing-up years?

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: What about management of expectations of the child and also their psychological and mental well-being?

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Will there be any involvement of the Ministry on these grounds?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I think the Member alludes – I may be wrong – in part, to concerns that the child who is brought up by two parents in Singapore who are of the same gender may result in this child having difficulties adjusting to mainstream society in schools and preschools, in the working environment, and so on and so forth.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But whether or not MSF needs to then come in to monitor and provide surveillance on the child, it is something quite altogether different.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Certainly, for any child, or any children in Singapore for whom legitimate concerns are raised about their welfare, then MSF will come in and take a look.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This child that has hitherto been taken care of by the biological father and his male partner, we are concerned about the formation and mainstreaming of same-sex parent family units in Singapore, but when it comes to the welfare of the child, we have to act on the basis of whether there are concerns or otherwise.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: But to resort to commercial surrogacy where you are paying for a womb overseas, renting a womb, does bring about ethical concerns.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: And there is always the option in Singapore for a married man and woman to explore adoption.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: So, there is an adoption of another child.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: So, there is a route to create a family unit with children.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Certainly, the Member is quite right that adoption of unrelated children or even of related children who had to be given up by other family members is and remains an option.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, ultimately, the concerns over surrogacy as well as commercial surrogacy remain.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In some jurisdictions, they have permitted altruistic surrogacy.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In others, they go the whole hog to allow commercial surrogacy.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And in some jurisdictions, they say they have put in safeguards to ensure that those who step forward to offer surrogate services are not exploited.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But we need to study this holistically and see what works for Singapore and what Singapore's broader society is prepared to accept or not to accept.
